_checks_comment: Review rules, in the same expression language as the lines. `when` is the
condition under which something is WRONG. Errors block filing; warnings are
things that are possible but usually mistakes; info is worth knowing.
A rule that cannot distinguish a mistake from a legitimate case must be a
warning, never an error -- blocking a correct return is worse than nagging.

checks.message: Your CPP contributions are larger than your employment income.
checks.help: One of the two boxes has been mistyped. CPP contributions come from box 16 of your T4; employment income is box 14.

checks.message: Your RRSP deduction is larger than your total income.
checks.help: An RRSP deduction cannot take your income below zero. Claim what you can this year; the rest carries forward and can be deducted in a later year.

checks.message: Your CPP contributions are above the maximum for one employer in 2025.
checks.help: This is normal if you worked for more than one employer — enter the real total and the over-contribution comes back to you on this return. If you had one employer, re-check box 16.

checks.message: Your second CPP contributions are above the 2025 maximum.
checks.help: Check box 16A. As with box 16, more than one employer can legitimately push this over the maximum.

checks.message: Your EI premiums are above the maximum for one employer in 2025.
checks.help: Normal with more than one employer; the excess is refunded on this return. With a single employer, re-check box 18.

checks.message: You have employment income but no CPP contributions.
checks.help: Box 16 may have been missed. It is legitimately blank if you were under 18, over 70, or had elected to stop contributing.

checks.message: You have employment income but no EI premiums.
checks.help: Box 18 may have been missed. It is legitimately blank if your work was not insurable — for example if you control more than 40% of the company's voting shares.

checks.message: Your RRSP deduction is higher than this year's income alone would allow.
checks.help: That is fine if you are using room carried forward from earlier years. Confirm the figure against the RRSP deduction limit on your latest notice of assessment — over-contributing attracts a penalty.

checks.message: Your child care claim was capped at two thirds of your earned income.
checks.help: That is the rule, not an error. Earned income means employment plus net self-employment income. In a couple the lower earner must claim child care, which is exactly when this cap bites — the rest of what you paid cannot be deducted by either of you.

checks.message: Your child care claim was capped by the per-child annual limits.
checks.help: Each child carries their own cap — $8,000 under 7, $5,000 from 7 to 16, $11,000 if eligible for the disability tax credit. Anything above the total cannot be claimed.

checks.message: Child care expenses were entered but no children.
checks.help: The deduction is limited by each child's own annual cap, so with no dependants listed the claim is zero. Add the children on the Dependants step.

checks.message: The amount for an eligible dependant does not apply when you have a spouse.
checks.help: You claim the spouse or common-law partner amount instead. Only one of the two is available.

checks.message: More than half of your eligible pension income has been split to your spouse.
checks.help: Form T1032 allows at most 50% of eligible pension income to be allocated.

checks.message: Some tuition could not be used this year and carries forward.
checks.help: Write the carry-forward figure down. Freshet does not yet track amounts between tax years, so next year's return will need it entered by hand.

checks.message: Nothing was withheld at source, so the full amount is payable when you file.
checks.help: If this happens again next year, CRA may ask you to pay by quarterly instalments.

checks.message: No income has been entered yet.
checks.help: A return with no income can still be worth filing — it is what establishes benefit and credit entitlements such as the GST/HST credit.

checks.message: Part of your home office expenses could not be deducted this year.
checks.help: The business-use-of-home deduction cannot create a loss. The excess carries forward against future business income — record the figure, because Freshet does not yet track amounts between tax years.

checks.message: Selling business assets has produced recaptured capital cost allowance.
checks.help: You sold for more than the pool's remaining tax value, so depreciation you deducted in earlier years is added back to this year's business income. It is expected, not a mistake.

checks.message: A terminal loss has been claimed on a class you have emptied.
checks.help: The value left in the pool when the last asset goes is deductible in full. Confirm the class really is empty — a terminal loss cannot be claimed while any asset remains in it.

checks.message: You are claiming less capital cost allowance than you could.
checks.help: That is a legitimate choice — the unclaimed amount stays in the pool and can be deducted in a later year, which is usually better when this year's income is already covered by your personal amounts. Check the planner on the return summary before deciding.

checks.message: The Ontario health premium has been added to your Ontario tax.
checks.help: It is charged on taxable income on a fixed scale above $20,000, and it is added after your credits rather than reduced by them — so it applies even when the rest of your Ontario tax is nil.

lines.label: Employment income
lines.note: Box 14 of every T4 slip.

lines.label: Other pensions and superannuation
lines.note: Registered pension plan payments, and — at 65 or older — RRIF and annuity income.

lines.label: Elected split-pension amount
lines.note: Pension income your spouse elected to move to your return under form T1032.

lines.label: Class 8 balance after additions and dispositions
lines.note: May go negative — that is recapture, not an error.

lines.label: Class 8 recapture
lines.note: Selling for more than the pool's remaining value claws back depreciation already deducted. It is income, not a smaller deduction.

lines.label: Class 8 terminal loss
lines.note: When the last asset in a class goes and value remains in the pool, the remainder is deductible in full — but only once the class is empty.

lines.label: Class 8 base for capital cost allowance
lines.note: A pool in recapture or wound up by a terminal loss has no balance left to depreciate.

lines.label: Capital cost allowance, class 8 — furniture, fixtures and general equipment

lines.note: May go negative — that is recapture, not an error.

lines.label: Class 10 terminal loss
lines.note: When the last asset in a class goes and value remains in the pool, the remainder is deductible in full — but only once the class is empty.

lines.label: Class 10 base for capital cost allowance
lines.note: A pool in recapture or wound up by a terminal loss has no balance left to depreciate.

lines.label: Capital cost allowance, class 10 — most motor vehicles

lines.note: May go negative — that is recapture, not an error.

lines.label: Class 12 terminal loss
lines.note: When the last asset in a class goes and value remains in the pool, the remainder is deductible in full — but only once the class is empty.

lines.label: Class 12 base for capital cost allowance
lines.note: A pool in recapture or wound up by a terminal loss has no balance left to depreciate.

lines.label: Capital cost allowance, class 12 — tools under the cost threshold, and software
Class 50 balance after additions and dispositions
lines.note: May go negative — that is recapture, not an error.

lines.label: Class 50 recapture
lines.note: Selling for more than the pool's remaining value claws back depreciation already deducted. It is income, not a smaller deduction.

lines.label: Class 50 terminal loss
lines.note: When the last asset in a class goes and value remains in the pool, the remainder is deductible in full — but only once the class is empty.

lines.label: Class 50 base for capital cost allowance
lines.note: A pool in recapture or wound up by a terminal loss has no balance left to depreciate.

lines.label: Capital cost allowance, class 50 — computer hardware and systems software
Class 10.1 cost, capped at the passenger vehicle limit
lines.note: Anything paid above the limit is simply not depreciable.

lines.label: Class 10.1 base for capital cost allowance
Capital cost allowance, class 10.1 — passenger vehicle above the cost limit
lines.note: Neither recapture nor a terminal loss ever arises on class 10.1, however the vehicle is sold.

lines.label: Capital cost allowance claimed
lines.note: CCA is discretionary: any amount from nil up to the maximum. Claiming less leaves the balance in the pool for a later year, which is worth doing when this year's income is already covered by personal amounts.

lines.label: Total recapture of capital cost allowance
Business-use-of-home expenses claimed
lines.note: This deduction cannot create or increase a business loss, so it is capped at whatever income survives every other expense.

lines.label: Business-use-of-home expenses carried forward
lines.note: Not lost — it can be deducted against business income in a later year. Freshet does not yet carry amounts between years, so record it.

lines.label: Net self-employment income
lines.note: Gross income less expenses, capital cost allowance and the allowable business-use-of-home portion, from form T2125. A loss is legitimate and reduces other income, so this line is not floored at zero.

lines.label: Net professional income
lines.note: Fees from a professional practice, less expenses. Form T2125, professional part. Capital cost allowance and business-use-of-home attach to the business activity at line 13500; include any depreciation for this activity in its expenses.

lines.label: Net farming income
lines.note: Form T2042. The optional inventory adjustment and the cash method are not modelled. Capital cost allowance and business-use-of-home attach to the business activity at line 13500; include any depreciation for this activity in its expenses.

lines.label: Net fishing income
lines.note: Form T2121. Capital cost allowance and business-use-of-home attach to the business activity at line 13500; include any depreciation for this activity in its expenses.

lines.label: Total net self-employment income
lines.note: Every activity together. This is what CPP is charged on, and what counts as working income for the Workers Benefit and as earned income for the child care cap.

lines.label: Pensionable earnings already covered by employment
lines.note: Reverse-engineered from the CPP withheld on the T4, so self-employment only contributes on what is left under the ceiling.

lines.label: Self-employment earnings subject to CPP
lines.note: The basic exemption is treated as used up by employment when there is any, and applied here otherwise. Combined pensionable earnings cannot exceed the annual ceiling.

lines.label: Base CPP on self-employment, both halves
lines.note: A self-employed person is both employee and employer, so they pay twice the employee rate.

lines.label: Enhanced CPP on self-employment, both halves
Deduction for CPP on self-employment income
lines.note: The employer half is a deduction; the employee half is a credit at line 31000. Splitting them this way is what keeps a self-employed person even with an employee.

lines.label: Base CPP contributions on self-employment income
RRSP deduction
lines.note: Contributions made in the year or in the first 60 days after year end.

lines.label: Deduction for CPP enhanced contributions
lines.note: The enhanced portion of CPP is deducted from income; the base portion is a credit instead.

lines.label: Deduction for elected split-pension amount
lines.note: The mirror of your spouse's line 11600: income you elected to move to their return.

lines.label: Child care limit from the children themselves
lines.note: Each child carries their own annual cap, and the caps add together.

lines.label: Child care limit from earned income
lines.note: Two thirds of earned income. Employment income is used as the proxy; self-employment is not modelled yet.

lines.label: Child care expenses
lines.note: A deduction, not a credit — and one the lower-income spouse must claim, which is why Freshet does not treat it as a choice.

lines.label: Basic personal amount
lines.note: Phased down for high incomes, on a straight line between the 29% and 33% bracket thresholds.

lines.label: Spouse or common-law partner amount
lines.note: Whatever your partner's own income does not already use up. Phased down for high income the same way the basic personal amount is.

lines.label: Medical expenses claimed
lines.note: A couple pools medical expenses on one return. Usually the lower-income partner, because the threshold that is subtracted is smaller.

lines.label: Amount for an eligible dependant
lines.note: For someone supporting a dependant without a spouse — a single parent, typically. It cannot be combined with the spouse amount, so it is zero whenever a partner is present.

lines.label: Canada caregiver amount for infirm children under 18
Canada caregiver amount for other infirm dependants 18 or older
lines.note: A different provision from the amount for infirm children under 18, and reduced by the dependant's own income. One dependant is supported; several are not.

lines.label: Age amount
lines.note: For anyone 65 or older on December 31, reduced by 15% of net income above the threshold. Moving income to a spouse can restore part of it.

lines.label: Pension income amount
lines.note: Up to $2,000 of eligible pension income. Split-pension income received counts only if the spouse who sent it was eligible, which is why a split can create a second one of these.

lines.label: Credit amounts before tuition
lines.note: Intermediate. Tuition is applied last because it is the amount that can be carried forward or transferred, so it should be the one left over.

lines.label: Tuition amount claimed by the student
Tuition available to transfer
lines.note: Capped at $5,000 of the current year's fees, federally.

lines.label: Tuition carried forward to a later year
lines.note: Not yet tracked between years. Record this figure — a later return will need it.

lines.label: Amounts available to transfer to your spouse
lines.note: Schedule 2. Age, pension and disability amounts you cannot use yourself, plus transferable tuition.

lines.label: Amounts transferred from your spouse
lines.note: Schedule 2. What your partner could not use themselves.

lines.label: Credit amounts at the lowest rate
Donations and gifts
lines.note: Credited at a higher rate above the first $200, which is why a couple should pool donations onto one return rather than splitting them.

lines.label: Ontario spouse or common-law partner amount
lines.note: Ontario reduces a base amount by the dependant's income and then caps the result, so the base exceeds the maximum. That gap is a band of the dependant's income that costs the claim nothing — a shape the federal equivalent does not share.

lines.label: Ontario amount for an eligible dependant
lines.note: Ontario reduces a base amount by the dependant's income and then caps the result, so the base exceeds the maximum. That gap is a band of the dependant's income that costs the claim nothing — a shape the federal equivalent does not share.

lines.label: Ontario caregiver amount
lines.note: Worksheet ON428: a $26,562 base reduced by the dependant's income and capped at $6,008. The previous model treated it as an amount reduced above a threshold, which is a different curve entirely.

lines.label: Ontario tuition amount claimed by the student
lines.note: Ontario abolished the tuition and education amounts for studies after 5 September 2017, so current-year fees earn no Ontario credit and none can be transferred. Only pre-2017 carryforward survives, and this model does not track it — which understates rather than overstates, the only safe direction to be wrong in.

lines.label: Ontario tuition available to transfer
lines.note: Ontario abolished the tuition and education amounts for studies after 5 September 2017, so current-year fees earn no Ontario credit and none can be transferred. Only pre-2017 carryforward survives, and this model does not track it — which understates rather than overstates, the only safe direction to be wrong in.

lines.label: Ontario amounts available to transfer to your spouse
Ontario amounts transferred from your spouse
Ontario surtax
lines.note: Ontario taxes its own tax: 20% of the amount above the first threshold, plus a further 36% above the second.

lines.label: Ontario tax reduction amounts
lines.note: Basic reduction plus an amount for each dependent child and each dependant with an impairment. In a couple only the higher earner may claim the dependant amounts, which the coupled solver enforces.

lines.label: Ontario tax reduction
lines.note: Twice the reduction amounts less the tax itself. The effect is that tax is eliminated entirely below the reduction amount and tapers to nothing at twice it, rather than being a flat credit.

lines.label: Ontario health premium
lines.note: Line 89. Added to Ontario tax rather than deducted, and charged on taxable income regardless of what credits reduced the tax to. Expressed as five clamped ramps; the chart's flat plateaus fall out of the arithmetic.

lines.label: Ontario tax
lines.note: Tax after the surtax and the reduction, plus the health premium, in that order.

lines.label: Total income tax deducted at source
CPP overpayment
lines.note: More than one employer each withhold up to their own maximum, so the excess is refunded here rather than being an error on the slips.

lines.label: Adjusted family income for the CARE credit
lines.note: Both partners' net income. For a single filer the household figure is absent, so their own net income stands in.

lines.label: Ontario CARE credit rate
lines.note: A step function: the rate drops two points for each whole or partial band above each tier floor, which is why it is computed with a ceiling rather than interpolated.

lines.label: Ontario Childcare Access and Relief from Expenses (CARE) credit
lines.note: Refundable — it is paid even when no tax is owing. Claimed by whoever claims the child care deduction.

lines.label: Workers Benefit is on a family basis
lines.note: A spouse or a dependant child moves the benefit to the larger family amounts and the later phase-out.

lines.label: Working income for the Workers Benefit
lines.note: Employment income. Self-employment is not modelled yet and would add to this.

lines.label: Adjusted income for the Workers Benefit
Workers Benefit, disability supplement
lines.note: Phases out later than the basic amount, so it survives a little further up the income scale.

lines.label: Canada Workers Benefit
lines.note: Refundable, and aimed at low working income — it is paid on the strength of working, not on tax owed. Only one spouse claims it for a couple.

lines.label: Refundable credits
lines.note: Paid to you whether or not you owe tax, unlike the non-refundable credits above.

lines.label: Total credits and tax already paid
